steps.speaker: Student A
steps.content: Hey, have you heard? That Iron from the neurosurgery department refused the offers of every major hospital! She said she's going to Syndicate to treat Mania!

steps.speaker: Student B
steps.content: Mania? Hasn't that already been determined to be a terminal illness with no cure?

steps.speaker: Student A
steps.content: Yeah, and it's a disease that only those Syndicate hood rats get. It's their karmic retribution!

steps.speaker: Student B
steps.content: Syndicate... ugh, even thinking about that place makes me want to puke.

steps.speaker: Student A
steps.content: Tsk tsk, we lowly mortals simply can't fathom the mind of a genius from a medical heritage. Guess we are not worthy of working with her in Eastside.

steps.speaker: Student B
steps.content: Hey, do you think genius Iron will turn into some wretched monster too after going to Syndicate?

steps.speaker: Student A
steps.content: Hahahaha, what did she call it? To sacrifice for one's ideals? Oh yes, noble ideals...

I could hear all their sneers and taunts. The onslaught of scorn never stopped from the moment I decided to treat Mania. Those self-righteous med students at Banyan mocked me mercilessly, even as I took to the stage to speak on their behalf.
Of course, I was self-righteous, too.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Greetings, dear teachers and fellow students. I'm Iron, valedictorian of this year's graduating class.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: It is the graduation ceremony of Banyan Medical College today. As the lucky beneficiaries of Eastside's elite medical education, we'll soon be applying the clinical knowledge we've learned to treating diseases and saving lives.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Someday, most of us will become the pillars of DisCity's health system, but...

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: I have no faith in such a future.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: How can a bunch of doctors who abandoned Syndicate, ignored the plight of thousands, and turned a deaf ear to the Mania spreading across DisCity, expect trust from their patients?

steps.speaker: Student A
steps.content: What kind of crazy nonsense is she spewing this time?

steps.speaker: Student B
steps.content: Whoa, is her M-value already spiking up before she even steps her foot in Syndicate?
I shared years of my research and analysis of Mania and the danger of its spread, but no one in the audience cared.
I did elicit an uproar. Not because they realized the severity and danger of Mania, but because they thought what I said, and myself, was a joke.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: According to my research, even though Mania is greatly affected by M-value, in essence it is still a communicable disease.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: My father always said that a doctor's duty is to fight diseases. Are we going to give up Mania research just because it's known as a terminal illness?

steps.speaker: Principal
steps.content: Ms. Iron, this is not the speech we agreed upon.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Even a hoodlum has the right to live. And this is not just a problem for Syndicate. Sooner or later it will become a problem for Eastside, and even all of DisCity.

steps.speaker: Principal
steps.content: Ms. Iron!

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: The destiny of mankind is a shared one. If we allow Mania to spread or even mutate into other forms, everyone here will turn into a Corruptor someday!

steps.speaker: Principal
steps.content: Enough!
I was ushered off the stage before I could finish my speech. Now that I think about it, it was probably just a meaningless, impulsive outburst, venting my youthful indignation.

steps.speaker: Hoodlum
steps.content: Show me who dares to open a clinic on the boss's turf?

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Those here for medical treatment, line up and take a number. The elderly, the disabled and the pregnant, go to the front of the line. Troublemakers, buzz off.

steps.speaker: Hoodlum
steps.content: Wow, newcomer to Syndicate and you already have the gall to act so tough. See if you can keep that attitude up in front of my fists.
I didn't have my power back then. It was harder than I imagined to gain a foothold in that unfamiliar city of disorder.
But gang warfare was just one of many problems. It was the endless cycle of violence that really brought the treatment of Mania to an impasse.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: Dr. Iron, please, please save my child! He's been running a high fever ever since he got caught in that crossfire...

steps.speaker: Gang member
steps.content: Outta my way, you old broad! I came here first! Save me first! Their Mania weapons are just too... ahhh!

steps.speaker: Hoodlum
steps.content: Why are more and more markings showing up on my body?! ****! Aren't you a professional doctor from Eastside?! Find a way to save me! I... I don't want to turn into a monster!
I used to hate my colleagues' "little white lies." I thought those were just fig leaves for their incompetence. Yet now, I was drained of all my energy just to ease their pain.
"Save lives"? Something so natural for doctors was a luxury here in Syndicate.
I became impatient. Mania research was at a bottleneck. As long as the thirst for harm and violence still existed, there would be no end to such chaos.

steps.speaker: Zoya
steps.content: Syndicate doesn't have any proper medical institutions, nor any professional staff. You want to treat Maniacs here? You can't do it alone.

steps.speaker: Zoya
steps.content: How about you join the Legion?
She gave a lucrative offer that was even more enticing than the FAC's offer today.
But I knew very well that the woman in front of me was a source of Syndicate's incessant warfare. I refused to fight fire with fire.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Since there's no professional staff, I'll pick and train some myself. Since there are no medical institutions, I'll set up the only neutral organization here.
In the end, she didn't force me. But after she left, the harassment of the clinic by other gangs eased markedly.
But as old problems were resolved, new problems arose.

steps.speaker: Youth
steps.content: Doctor... your left hand... has the same Mania markings as I do...

steps.speaker: Youth
steps.content: So you have been infected as well...?

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Given the Chief's generosity toward the Bureau's employees, it's only natural that you would be reluctant to give up your current position, Miss. How about this...
When I came back to my senses, I had already pressed my scalpel against the kid's artery.
It was not the first time that I lost control of my emotions. My rage cost me quite a few pieces of equipment. I could not put my patients at risk. I had to temporarily close down the clinic.
It seemed that my journey to treat Mania and save Syndicate was coming to an end too.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Today is the eleventh day of my Mania infection. My symptoms... include a severe headache, twitching of the limbs, poor coordination, and a strong burning sensation in the left arm.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: I lost consciousness for two hours and tried to break open the clinic door to go out and harm others.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: My stock of painkillers has been exhausted, and when I tried to call the major hospitals in Eastside and medical departments of DisCity... my signal was blocked...

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: I predict that the Mania contamination in my left arm will spread to my heart in... two days...
I no longer had the strength to write, so I had to log my daily symptoms with audio recordings. There was an unprecedented downpour that night, so the recording wasn't clear.
Though I didn't contribute much to curing Mania, it might be helpful for others to leave behind a detailed case record...
I thought I'd get through that long night alone, just like the past ten days...
Is anyone here? There's a child who needs medical help!
Please, I beg you, open the door!

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: The clinic is closed and not operating.
Please, just give us a bottle of medicine! Any medicine is fine!

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: You can't just use some random medicine... Tell me the symptoms and I'll make a diagnosis.
She... she is a Corruptor... she just mutated half an hour ago.
But trust me, she's in a coma and doesn't threaten anyone. Her pulse... is very weak.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Sssss—
Are you alright? Sounds like you're in pain.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: It's nothing. I haven't been in contact with anyone for too long. I almost...
I almost opened the door and let out all my rage of incompetence on them.
If it's really too difficult for you, can you point us towards a nearby hospital? A pharmacy would be good, too...
Please... her only wish is to live...
Hospital? Pharmacy? Those don't exist in Syndicate. It's raining so heavily. They had nowhere else to go.
I was the only one stupid enough to do those things in Syndicate. Mania, it was all on me...

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Give me five minutes, please. I'll open the door for you.
Amputation is a piece of cake, but this was the first time I'm amputating myself.
The hand is the soul of the surgeon.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: I'm ready. Bring her in.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: You... must stop the bleeding quickly!
I must have startled her when I opened the door looking like that.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: It's alright. I can tough it out. The medicine in the clinic is running out. Give them to her first.
Unfortunately, the child named Paige didn't make it past dawn. But I overcame Mania and became a Sinner.
My M-value temporarily stopped growing because of my will to resist... Then perhaps Mania could be controlled by curbing the urge for violence.
I could only perfect such an unprecedented type of surgery through trial and error.

steps.speaker: Gangster
steps.content: Wanna hear something hot off the press?

steps.speaker: Hoodlum
steps.content: Another gang scandal?

steps.speaker: Gangster
steps.content: No! Do you remember that Eastside doctor named Iron?

steps.speaker: Hoodlum
steps.content: That dud who kept talking about curing Mania? she's just a scammer from Eastside if you ask me. She hasn't been showing up for a long time, what happened?

steps.speaker: Gangster
steps.content: Her clinic reopened under the new name SALVA! The strange thing is, she took in many Maniacs, but when they left they were all brain-dead!

steps.speaker: Gangster
steps.content: They were all just stuttering about, looking dumb. They don't laugh or cry or know anything, so much that they don't even look human anymore. I'd say it's a life worse than death!

steps.speaker: Hoodlum
steps.content: My ***! And they call it SALVA? More like SAVAGE! What about Mania, then? Can it really be cured?

steps.speaker: Gangster
steps.content: Ha, what kind of place do you think this is? So what if you are cured. You'll get infected again anyway!

steps.speaker: Gangster
steps.content: But that's not all! I heard that Iron replaced her left arm with a robotic one. And everyone is saying that she is literally no longer human!

steps.speaker: Hoodlum
steps.content: Then what is she now?

steps.speaker: Gangster
steps.content: A monster! A cold monster more ruthless than any Corruptor!
On the way back, Iron keeps staring at her left arm, deep in thought.
Are you upset by their insults?

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: If I cared about that, SALVA would have long ceased to exist.
At least you can explain to them that nerve modification surgery is the only option.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Explain? My requirements for the FAC are the same as the ones I have for myself. I value results over verbal promises.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: I can suppress one's Mania and extend one's life. That should be a good enough explanation in and of itself. If it's not enough to persuade some people, I don't want to waste my breath on them.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: And they got one thing right. I am a cold monster. Only a cold surgical machine can save a place like Syndicate.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Warmth will only render one unable to make decisions at critical times.

options: I can't be so cold and ruthless like you talked about
I don't think you have no warmth

choices.text: I can't be so cold and ruthless like you talked about
I don't think you have no warmth

steps.content: It's precisely because there's warmth in people, that they have emotions and compassion.
You said that you could tell I wanted to save lives. You were putting trust in my warmth, weren't you?

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Think what you will.
Then why do you save people, Dr. Iron? Surely not because you're "cold"?
It is precisely because you're warm towards every person that you want to save every life.
Even if a certain life is meaningless in the eyes of others, you are unwilling to let it perish.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Don't assume that you know me well.
But you didn't refute me either.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Heh...
Iron gazes down at her right hand, releasing and then re-clenching it.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Even I can't save everyone.

options: That's why you need support from the FAC

choices.text: That's why you need support from the FAC

steps.content: That's why you let me watch the surgery up close, right?
Personnel, technical and financial support... These can all definitely help you. Going about it alone is not good for your M-value.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: You've seen the surgery already. Do you still not understand? You had a hard time keeping up with just your eyes. Imagine if you had to keep up with your hands! At present, the most critical part of this treatment is the surgeon's skills.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Aside from me, there are no other surgeons who can perform such a complicated procedure in DisCity. Besides, my future goal is the possibility of full recovery after a patient's Manic tumors are removed. That will require even higher skills.
So what you're saying is, the FAC should first train doctors who are willing to treat Mania?

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: How many do you think will voluntarily step up to the challenge?

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Mania has been spreading for a long time, but Syndicate has ever only had one proper clinic.
Even in the FAC, which you regard as incompetent, there are people like the 6th Squadron, like Claire.
Mania is not just a crisis for Syndicate, but one that threatens all of DisCity, and even the fate of humanity.
I'm sure there will be people who are willing to step up, just like you did back then.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Hahahaha...
What's so funny?

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: You're very much like me from before... but you're luckier than I was back then.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: You have many friends, and that's why you're willing to believe in the good in humanity.
Now you have a friend, too.
She pushes up her glasses. The reflection of the lenses conceals the trace of earnest sincerity behind her scoff.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Alright, you lackey Chief. No need to butter me up. I haven't promised to work with you or the FAC.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: You only saved a roomful of people. Don't get too cocky.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: I want to save all of Syndicate.
